literal: The Rouran flee far; before you gain nothing, behind you the trouble of southern invasion—this is a perilous course."
idiomatic: "The Rouran flee far—you gain nothing ahead while southern invasion threatens behind. That is a perilous course."

literal: Hao said: "If this year you do not crush the Rouran, you cannot defend against the southern bandits.
idiomatic: Hao said, "If we do not crush the Rouran this year, we cannot defend against the southern enemy."

literal: Since the state annexed the western kingdom, southerners have feared and raised voices and moved hosts to guard the Huai north.
idiomatic: "Since the state annexed the western kingdom, the south has lived in fear, raising alarms and moving armies to guard the Huai north."

literal: They north, we south; they campaign, we rest—the situation is so.
idiomatic: "They are north, we south; they campaign, we rest—that is the pattern."

literal: Break the Rouran in the north and in the going and returning you therefore do not see them arrive.
idiomatic: "Break the Rouran in the north and, in the going and returning, you will not see them arrive."

literal: How so?
idiomatic: "How so?"

literal: Liu Yu took Guanzhong, left his beloved son, several tens of thousands of elite troops and fierce generals and strong soldiers—yet could not hold firm; the whole army perished and the sound of wailing has not ceased to this day.
idiomatic: "Liu Yu took Guanzhong, left his beloved son, tens of thousands of elite troops and fierce commanders—yet could not hold it. The whole army was lost and the sound of wailing has not ceased to this day."

literal: How, just when the state is in its brilliant age and horses and men are strong, can you set a foal's teeth against a tiger's maw?
idiomatic: "How, in the state's brilliant age with strong horses and men, can you set a foal's teeth against a tiger's maw?"

literal: Suppose the state gave them the lands south of the Yellow River—they could certainly not hold them.
idiomatic: "Suppose we gave them the lands south of the Yellow River—they could not hold them."

literal: Measuring that they cannot hold, they therefore will certainly not come.
idiomatic: "Knowing they cannot hold them, they will certainly not come."

literal: If they have a host, it is only border-guard troops.
idiomatic: "If they field troops at all, it will be only border guards."

literal: See water in a bottle freeze and know the cold of all under heaven;
idiomatic: "See water freeze in a bottle and know the cold of all under heaven."

literal: taste one slice of meat and know the flavor in the cauldron.
idiomatic: "Taste one slice of meat and know the flavor in the cauldron."

literal: Things have their kind; one can infer and obtain.
idiomatic: "Things have their kind—you can infer from one to all."

literal: Moreover the Rouran rely on distance and think the state's strength cannot reach them; they have relaxed themselves a long time.
idiomatic: "The Rouran rely on distance and think the empire cannot reach them—they have grown complacent a long while."

literal: Therefore in summer they scatter the host and release herds; when autumn fat comes they gather, turning their backs to cold and faces to warmth, coming south to raid.
idiomatic: "In summer they scatter herds; when autumn fat comes they gather, turning from cold toward warmth and raiding south."

literal: Now strike them unprepared; the great army arrives suddenly—they will surely be terrified and flee at the sight of dust.
idiomatic: "Strike them unprepared now. The great army arrives suddenly—they will flee in terror at the sight of dust."

literal: Stallions guard the herds, mares cling to foals;
idiomatic: "Stallions guard the herds, mares cling to foals."

literal: driven in flight they are hard to control, cannot obtain grass and water;
idiomatic: "Driven in flight they are hard to control and cannot find grass and water."

literal: within a few days they cluster in exhaustion and weakness and can be destroyed in one stroke.
idiomatic: "Within days they cluster, exhausted and weak, and can be destroyed in one stroke."

literal: Brief toil for lasting ease—the time cannot be lost.
idiomatic: "Brief toil for lasting ease—the moment cannot be lost."

literal: Only I fear the ruler above lacks this intent.
idiomatic: "Only I fear the throne lacks this intent."

literal: Now the sage mind is decided—how can it be stopped?"
idiomatic: "Now the sage mind is decided—how can it be stopped?"

literal: They then set out.
idiomatic: They then marched.

literal: The Celestial Master said to Hao: "Can this campaign succeed?"
idiomatic: The Celestial Master asked Hao, "Will this campaign succeed?"

literal: Hao said: "It will surely conquer.
idiomatic: Hao said, "It will surely conquer."

literal: Only I fear the generals will be petty, looking before and behind, unable to press the victory deep, so that the whole cannot be taken."
idiomatic: "Only I fear the generals will be petty, looking before and behind, unable to press the victory deep, so the whole prize cannot be taken."

literal: When the army arrived and entered their territory, the Rouran at first made no preparations.
idiomatic: When the army entered their territory, the Rouran at first made no preparations.

literal: They then divided the army to search: five thousand li east and west, three thousand li north and south; captives and livestock, carts and tents gained numbered in the millions.
idiomatic: They divided the army to search five thousand li east and west and three thousand li north and south. Captives and livestock, carts and tents taken numbered in the millions.

literal: Gaoche who killed Rouran kin and came over numbered more than three hundred thousand clans.
idiomatic: Gaoche who killed Rouran kin and surrendered numbered more than three hundred thousand clans.

literal: The barbarians then scattered in disorder.
idiomatic: The Rouran then scattered in disorder.

literal: The emperor followed the Ruoshui west to Zhuoye Mountain; the great generals indeed feared deep advance and ambush and urged the emperor to stop.
idiomatic: The emperor followed the Ruoshui west to Zhuoye Mountain. The great generals feared ambush in a deep advance and urged him to stop.

literal: The Celestial Master, because of Hao's words of other days, firmly urged the emperor to pursue to the end; the emperor would not listen.
idiomatic: The Celestial Master, citing Hao's earlier counsel, firmly urged pursuit to the end; the emperor would not listen.

literal: Later a surrendered man said: "The Rouran khan Datan had first fallen ill, not knowing what to do; he burned his tents, loaded carts himself, and with a hundred men entered the mountains and fled south.
idiomatic: Later a surrendered man said, "Khan Datan had fallen ill, not knowing what to do. He burned his tents, loaded carts, and with a hundred men fled south into the mountains."

literal: Men and livestock crowded together in an area sixty li square with no one to command them.
idiomatic: "Men and livestock crowded together in an area sixty li square with no one to command them."

literal: A hundred and eighty li apart, the pursuing army did not arrive; they then slowly fled west and only thus escaped.
idiomatic: "A hundred and eighty li away, the pursuing army did not arrive. They then fled west at leisure and only thus escaped."

literal: " Hearing a Liangzhou merchant Hu say: "If you had advanced two more days, you would have destroyed them utterly."
idiomatic: A Liangzhou merchant was heard to say, "Had you advanced two more days, you would have destroyed them utterly."

literal: The emperor deeply regretted it.
idiomatic: The emperor deeply regretted it.

literal: When the great army had returned, the southern army indeed could not move, as Hao had foreseen.
idiomatic: When the great army returned, the southern army indeed could not move—as Hao had foreseen.

literal: Hao clearly understood astronomy and loved to observe stellar changes.
idiomatic: Hao had a clear grasp of astronomy and loved to watch the stars.

literal: He often placed gold, silver, and copper awls in vinegar to turn them green; when he saw something at night he would use the awl to draw characters on paper and record the anomaly.
idiomatic: He often placed gold, silver, and copper styli in vinegar to turn them green; when he saw something at night he scratched characters on paper with a stylus to record the anomaly.

literal: Emperor Taiwu whenever he visited Hao's residence asked much about strange matters.
idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Taiwu visited Hao's house he asked much about strange matters.

literal: Sometimes in haste he could not gird his belt; Hao would present plain vegetable food, without time for refinement, and the emperor would lift spoon and chopsticks for him, or stand and taste and return.
idiomatic: Sometimes, in haste, Hao could not gird his belt and would offer plain vegetables without time to refine them; the emperor would lift spoon and chopsticks for him, or stand, taste, and leave.

literal: Such was the favor he enjoyed.
idiomatic: Such was the favor he enjoyed.

literal: He was then brought in and out of the sleeping quarters.
idiomatic: He was then admitted in and out of the imperial sleeping quarters.

literal: He was further made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Special Advance, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Left Grand Master of the Palace, to reward his stratagems.
idiomatic: He was further made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Special Advance, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Left Grand Master of the Palace to reward his stratagems.

literal: The emperor said at ease to Hao: "Your talent and wisdom are deep and broad; you served my grandfather and father, loyal through three generations—I therefore keep you near.
idiomatic: The emperor said gently to Hao, "Your talent and wisdom run deep. You served my grandfather and father with loyalty through three reigns, and I therefore keep you near."

literal: Think to exhaust remonstrance and counsel; do not harbor hidden thoughts.
idiomatic: "Give me your fullest remonstrance and counsel; hide nothing in your heart."

literal: Though I may at the time shift anger, if I do not use your words, in time could I not deeply consider what you say?"
idiomatic: "Though I may flare in anger and not heed you at once, in time might I not deeply weigh your words?"

literal: He then had singing craftsmen go through and praise the ministers—the matter is in the Biography of Changsun Daosheng.
idiomatic: He then had court musicians sing through praises of the ministers—the matter is recorded in the Biography of Changsun Daosheng.

literal: He also summoned several hundred newly surrendered Gaoche chieftains and bestowed food and drink before them.
idiomatic: He also summoned several hundred newly surrendered Gaoche chieftains and feasted them.

literal: Pointing to Hao to show them he said: "You all see this man—slender, frail, and weak, his hands unable to bend a bow or hold a spear—yet what he harbors in his breast surpasses armor and weapons.
idiomatic: Pointing at Hao he told them, "You see this man—slight, frail, unable to bend a bow or hold a spear—yet what he carries in his breast surpasses armor and arms."

literal: At first I had the will to campaign, yet feared I could not decide myself; the victories before and after were all because this man guided me to reach this point."
idiomatic: "At first I wished to campaign yet feared I could not decide alone. Every victory before and after came because this man guided me here."

literal: He then charged the Masters of Writing: "Whatever great plans of army and state you cannot decide, consult Hao first and then act."
idiomatic: He then charged the Masters of Writing, "Whatever great plans of army and state you cannot decide, consult Hao first, then act."

literal: Soon the southern frontier generals memorialized that Song troops wished to invade the lands south of the Yellow River and asked for thirty thousand men to strike them before they set out.
idiomatic: Soon the southern frontier generals reported that Song troops meant to invade the lands south of the Yellow River and asked for thirty thousand men to strike before they marched.

literal: They would also execute northerners south of the Yellow River living on the border, cut off their guides, enough to blunt their edge and make them not dare advance deep.
idiomatic: They would also execute northerners stranded on the border, cut off their guides, blunt the enemy's edge, and keep them from advancing deep.

literal: An edict ordered the ministers to debate; all said it should be granted.
idiomatic: An edict ordered debate among the ministers; all said it should be granted.

literal: Hao said: "This cannot be followed.
idiomatic: Hao said, "This must not be followed."

literal: In years past the state greatly broke the Rouran and horses still had strength.
idiomatic: "In years past the state shattered the Rouran and our horses still have strength."

literal: The southern bandits have lost their elite and constantly fear light troops arriving suddenly; therefore they raise voices and move hosts to guard against the unexpected—they do not dare strike first.
idiomatic: "The southern enemy has lost its elite and constantly fears sudden light attack. They raise alarms and move hosts to guard the unexpected—they do not dare strike first."

literal: Moreover the southern lands are low and wet; summer months are steaming hot—not the season for marching armies.
idiomatic: "The south is low and wet; summer months steam—not the season for armies."

literal: Moreover they have first made strict preparations and will surely hold the walls firm.
idiomatic: "They have already made strict preparations and will hold their walls firm."

literal: Station troops to attack and grain will not suffice;
idiomatic: "Station troops to attack and grain will not suffice."

literal: divide troops to raid widely and there will be none to meet the enemy.
idiomatic: "Divide troops to raid widely and there will be none to meet the enemy."

literal: I do not see the profit.
idiomatic: "I see no profit in it."

literal: Even if they can come, wait until they are weary; when autumn is cool and horses are fat, take food from the enemy and strike them slowly—the plan of complete safety.
idiomatic: "Even if they come, wait until they are weary. When autumn cools and horses grow fat, take food from the enemy and strike slowly—that is the plan of complete safety."

literal: The ministers at court and the northwestern frontier generals who followed Your Majesty in campaigns west destroyed Helian and north broke the Rouran, gaining many beautiful women and treasures, horses and herds in droves;
idiomatic: "Ministers at court and northwestern frontier generals who followed Your Majesty west destroyed Helian and north shattered the Rouran, gaining beautiful women, treasures, horses and herds in droves."

literal: the southern garrison generals, hearing, were envious and also wished to raid south for goods and wealth.
idiomatic: "Southern garrison generals, hearing this, grew envious and also wished to raid south for goods and wealth."

literal: Therefore they falsely inflate bandit strength, pluck hairs to seek flaws, hoping to indulge their hearts.
idiomatic: "Therefore they falsely inflate enemy strength and pluck hairs to seek flaws, hoping to indulge their hearts."

literal: Since they could not gain approval, they repeatedly report bandit movement to frighten the court.
idiomatic: "Denied approval, they repeatedly report enemy movement to frighten the court."

literal: Turning their backs on the public to serve private ends, creating trouble for the state—not loyalty.
idiomatic: "They turn their backs on the public to serve private ends and create trouble for the state—that is not loyalty."

literal: The emperor followed Hao's plan.
idiomatic: The emperor followed Hao's counsel.

literal: The southern garrison generals memorialized that bandits had arrived, yet themselves declared few troops and asked to select garrison troops south of Youzhou to assist defense.
idiomatic: The southern garrison generals reported enemies at hand yet declared themselves short of troops and asked to draw garrison forces south of Youzhou to reinforce them.

literal: They built boats on the Zhang River and made strict preparations.
idiomatic: They built boats on the Zhang River and made strict preparations.

literal: Those who debated among the ministers were unanimous, wishing to send five thousand cavalry and provisionally appoint Sima Chuzhi, Lu Gui, Han Yanzhi, and others to entice frontier people.
idiomatic: The debating ministers were unanimous, wishing to send five thousand cavalry and provisionally appoint Sima Chuzhi, Lu Gui, Han Yanzhi, and others to entice frontier people.

literal: Hao said: "This is not the upper stratagem.
idiomatic: Hao said, "This is not the best stratagem."

literal: When they hear that south of Youzhou elite troops have all been sent, great boat-building, light cavalry in the rear, wishing to establish Sima and exterminate the Song clan, they will surely be alarmed throughout the state, fearing destruction, and will send all elite strength to guard the northern border.
idiomatic: "When they hear elite troops south of Youzhou are all sent, great boat-building, light cavalry in the rear, and plans to establish Sima and exterminate the Song clan, they will be alarmed throughout the state, fear destruction, and send all elite strength to guard the northern border."

literal: Later learning the official army has sound without substance, relying on their prior gathering, they will surely be pleased and advance, coming straight to the river to indulge in outrage.
idiomatic: "Later, learning the official army has sound without substance, they will rely on their prior gathering, advance gladly, come straight to the river, and indulge in outrage."

literal: Then our defending generals will have nothing to resist them.
idiomatic: "Then our defending generals will have nothing with which to resist them."

literal: If they have men who see the moment, skilled in setting stratagems, seizing the interval to advance deep, fearing our state is empty, trouble is not hard to raise.
idiomatic: "If they have men who read the moment, skilled in stratagem, seizing the interval to advance deep while our state looks empty, trouble is not hard to raise."

literal: This is not a fine plan for controlling the enemy.
idiomatic: "That is not a fine plan for controlling the enemy."

literal: Now the ministers wish to repel bandits by might—that is precisely what summons them to come quickly.
idiomatic: "Now the ministers wish to repel the enemy by show of force—that is precisely what summons them quickly."

literal: To raise empty sound and summon real harm—this is what is meant.
idiomatic: "Raise empty sound and summon real harm—that is what is meant."

literal: You cannot fail to think; regret will come too late.
idiomatic: "You cannot fail to think—regret will come too late."

literal: Our envoys are there, due to return before the fourth month; you can wait until the envoys arrive and investigate before acting—still not late.
idiomatic: "Our envoys are there, due back before the fourth month. Wait until they return and investigate before acting—still not late."

literal: Chu's faction is what they hate—they will seize their state; how can they sit and watch?
idiomatic: "Chu's faction is what they hate—they will seize their state. How can they sit and watch?"

literal: Therefore when Chu goes they come; when Chu stops they rest—the situation is so.
idiomatic: "Therefore when Chu goes they come; when Chu stops they rest—that is the pattern."

literal: Moreover Chu and the rest are petty talents, able to gather the light and worthless but unable to achieve great merit.
idiomatic: "Moreover Chu and the rest are petty talents, able to gather the light and worthless but unable to achieve great merit."

literal: Creating trouble for the state, making arms link calamity—surely this crowd.
idiomatic: "Creating trouble for the state and linking arms to calamity—surely this crowd will do it."

literal: Your servant once heard Lu Gui persuade Yao Xing to let him enter Jingzhou.
idiomatic: "I once heard Lu Gui persuade Yao Xing to let him enter Jingzhou."

literal: When he arrived he scattered and was defeated and could not escape being seized and sold as slaves by barbarian bandits, bringing calamity on Yao Hong—a result already seen."
idiomatic: "When he arrived he scattered and was defeated, was seized and sold as slaves by barbarian bandits, and brought calamity on Yao Hong—an outcome already seen."

literal: Hao also stated that heaven's seasons were unfavorable to them, saying: "Now the baleful qi is in Yangzhou—one should not first raise arms.
idiomatic: Hao also argued that heaven's seasons favored the enemy, saying, "The baleful qi now sits in Yangzhou—one should not strike first. That is the first sign."

literal: A wuwu year punishes itself—whoever strikes first is wounded—second.
idiomatic: "A wuwu year punishes itself—whoever strikes first is wounded. That is the second."

literal: An eclipse extinguishes light; day is dim and stars appear; birds fall from flight; lodges correspond to Dipper and Ox—worry is in peril and ruin—third.
idiomatic: "An eclipse extinguishes light; day dims and stars appear; birds fall from the sky; lodges correspond to Dipper and Ox—worry lies in peril and ruin. That is the third."

literal: Mars hides in Wings and Axletree, warning of disorder and mourning—fourth.
idiomatic: "Mars hides in Wings and Axletree, warning disorder and mourning. That is the fourth."

literal: The White Star has not appeared—whoever advances is defeated—fifth.
idiomatic: "The White Star has not appeared—whoever advances is defeated. That is the fifth."

literal: The ruler who founds a state first cultivates human affairs, next exhausts earthly advantage, last observes heaven's seasons—therefore ten thousand acts and ten thousand successes, the state secure and the person flourishing.
idiomatic: "The ruler who founds a state first cultivates human affairs, next exhausts earthly advantage, last observes heaven's seasons—then ten thousand acts bring ten thousand successes, the state secure and the ruler flourishing."

literal: Now Song is a new state—human affairs are not complete;
idiomatic: "Song is a new state—human affairs are not complete."

literal: calamities and changes appear repeatedly—heaven's seasons are not in harmony;
idiomatic: "Calamities appear again and again—heaven's seasons are not in harmony."

literal: boats travel while waters dry—earthly advantage is not exhausted.
idiomatic: "Boats sail while waters dry—earthly advantage is not exhausted."
